claim: Consider any rooted ultrametric three-tip binary tree with sister leaves \(1,2\) and outgroup leaf \(3\), root-to-tip height \(H>0\) and a strictly internal sister-clade stem of length \(h\) with \(0<h<H\). For any two distinct strictly positive integer abundance profiles \(x=(a,b,c)\), \(y=(a\prime,b\prime,c\prime)\) having the same total census \(N\ge3\), compare expected rooted phylogenetic diversity \(P_m(x),P_m(y)\) under uniform sampling of \(m\) individuals without replacement. A double strict ranking reversal means that the sequence of nonzero signs of \(P_m(x)-P_m(y)\), for integer \(2\le m\le N-1\), changes sign at least twice. No such double reversal exists for \(N\le6\), for any permitted \(h/H\). At \(N=7\), exactly three unordered pairs of profile types (quotienting the sister-tip swap independently within each profile) admit double reversals. They are \((1,1,5)\) versus \((3,3,1)\) precisely for \(1/2<h/H<13/23\); \((1,2,4)\) versus \((3,3,1)\) precisely for \(1/7<h/H<3/17\); and \((1,4,2)\) versus \((3,3,1)\) precisely for \(1/5<h/H<3/13\). At the endpoints of these open intervals no double strict ranking reversal remains, even after omitting ties. For example with \(H=9\), \(h=2\), \(x=(1,4,2)\), \(y=(3,3,1)\), the expected-PD differences at sample sizes \(m=2,3,4,5,6\) are \((1/21,-1/35,-1/35,1/7,2/7)\), exhibiting the strict sign pattern \(+,-,-,+,+\). The theorem is an exact finite exhaustive classification with rational interval certificates valid for every real branch-length ratio \(0<h/H<1\); it does not claim a bound at larger censuses or for non-ultrametric trees.
integrity: All canonical abundance compositions through census seven are generated via two independent methods. Every same-census unordered pair is tested at every interior sampling depth across every exact real branch-length parameter interval and its rational endpoints; the hypergeometric edge formula is independently checked against direct enumeration of individual subsamples. Computer-assisted proof is finite and reproducible, not an assertion about larger censuses.
scientific_limitations: Exactly three strictly present taxa on one fixed rooted ultrametric tree, equal positive-integer censuses, uniform individual-based sampling without replacement. Only the sharp first double-reversal boundary through seven individuals is classified; larger censuses, non-ultrametric trees, extrapolation, sample uncertainty, and different sampling conventions are excluded.
title: Seven individuals are the sharp double-crossing boundary for ultrametric phylogenetic rarefaction
